videos.script: Prompt engineering lesson twenty-nine showed ReAct as a format: Thought, Action, Observation, and then an Answer. This lesson runs it as code, and watches where it breaks. {{title}} First in plain text, the way the paper did it. A model writes its thought and an action, and a parser reads them. {{text}} You will see a model write an observation it never received. A delivery date, invented, and a confident answer built on it. One line in the request stops that from happening: a stop sequence. {{stop}} Then the same loop with native tool calls, which is how agents are built today. The thought is a text block. The action is a structured request. An id ties each result to its call. {{native}} You will log every step to a file and read the run back, step by step. {{trace}} And you will watch a loop that would never end on its own: the same search, again and again. The host notices, and stops it. {{loop}}
